subject: IP custody ledger + firewall attestation for private endpoints
messages:
From: Eli Torres <security@borealishealth.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Request: IP custody ledger + firewall attestation for private endpoints

Markus,

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment topology last week. Our security team needs a concise artifact set to close our vendor risk review for the private endpoint integration. Specifically we need:

- A ledger of all egress IPs used by Redwood private control / data planes for our tenant (stable list + ephemerals) with ownership tags and assignment times.
- Firewall policy statement describing required inbound/outbound ports/FQDNs and whether SNI/TLS inspection or mTLS is needed.
- Evidence that egress telemetry (SNI, destination IPs, TCP port) is captured for at least 30 days for forensic purposes.
- Any documented fallback behaviors (e.g., regional failover, model variant fallbacks) that might change exit IPs.

Can you provide the artifacts or point us to the right place in your evidence bundle by EOD Friday (Dec 3)? We will use these to populate our SOC-ready checklist.

Appreciate it,
Eli Torres
Head of Vendor Security
Borealis Health

--
Attachments: none

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc:  eli@borealishealth.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: IP custody ledger + firewall attestation for private endpoints

Team — forwarding Eli's ask from Borealis. This is time-sensitive for their procurement gate. Quick plan:

1) Laura: generate a compact CSV ledger listing each IP / CIDR, first-seen and last-assigned timestamp, purpose (control-plane, data-plane, telemetry), and an ownership tag (redwood-managed / cloud-nat / customer-provided). Include a column "ephemeral_rotation_window" if applicable. Use the internal ledger template (SEC-LEDGER-v2).
2) Jordan: pull the firewall policy statement and produce a one-page attestation PDF that includes ports, FQDNs, TLS/SNI notes, and the default behavior for failover. Add a short section on telemetry retention and pointers to where logs are stored.
3) I'll coordinate packaging and a signed attestation (DocuSign) for Borealis. Also confirm whether any of the egress IPs are subject to rotation during regional failover (call that out explicitly).

Deadline: Dec 3 COB Pacific. Keep replies brief — we'll iterate offline.

-Markus

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Cc: Eli Torres <security@borealishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Request: IP custody ledger + firewall attestation for private endpoints

Markus / Jordan / Eli — attaching the first pass artifacts. Items included:

- egress-ip-ledger-v1.csv (attached) — columns: ip, cidr, assigned_since, last_seen, purpose, ownership, ephemeral_rotation_window_minutes, region, notes. Ledger contains 18 stable control-plane IPs and a pattern for ephemeral data-plane IP ranges generated from the customer-dedicated NAT pool.
- firewall-policy-attestation.pdf (attached) — one-page attestation describing required outbound ports (443 only for control plane; 443 + 80 for optional health checks), recommended FQDN allowlist (control.redwood-inference.com, telemetry.redwood-inference.com, model-catalog.redwood.ai), and notes on TLS fingerprinting vs SNI inspection. We state that mTLS is available for private control-plane websocket connections upon request and cite the config PR number.
- egress-telemetry-snippets.log (attached) — sample 7-day snippet of SNI and destination IPs (redacted tenant IDs) to show we capture the fields requested. Retention policy: telemetry stored for 90 days by default; logs are archived for 365 days for regulated customers on request.

A few clarifications to call out here:
- Ephemeral IP rotation: ephemeral data-plane IPs are allocated from a customer-specific NAT pool managed by the customer's VPC or by Redwood-managed NAT when requested. When Redwood-managed NAT is used, rotation is controlled by ops and scheduled; control-plane IPs are stable unless a region migration occurs (we list the migration fallback behavior in the attestation).
- Fallback behaviors: if a regional outage forces failover, outgoing egress may originate from the paired region's control-plane CIDR; those ranges are included in the ledger's "notes" column.

Next steps: Markus to review and sign the attestation. Jordan — please add the small section about rate-limit/traffic-class tagging (internal ops requirement) before final sign-off.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Product Security Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: egress-ip-ledger-v1.csv (csv, 12 KB); firewall-policy-attestation.pdf (pdf, 18 KB); egress-telemetry-snippets.log (log, 6 KB)

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai

Date: Thu, 2 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: IP custody ledger + firewall attestation for private endpoints

Eli — thanks for the patience. Laura and Jordan assembled the requested artifacts and I've reviewed them: ledger covers current stable control/data exit ranges, attestation includes fallback behavior and telemetry retention.

I signed the attestation and submitted a DocuSign envelope (link below) for Borealis legal to countersign. Quick notes for your team:
- Primary control-plane egress (stable): 18 IPs listed in ledger, allow outbound port 443 to control.redwood-inference.com.
- Data-plane exit behavior: either customer NAT or Redwood-managed NAT; when Redwood-managed NAT is used we provide scheduled rotation windows (we call those out in column ephemeral_rotation_window_minutes).
- Telemetry: SNI + dst IP + dst port captured; retention for default tenants is 90 days, longer available under contract.

DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/verify/XYZ-987
Drive bundle: https://drive.google.com/open?id=example-doc-link
Jira: SEC-3124

If Borealis requires additional cryptographic evidence (e.g., HSM-signed attestation), let us know and we'll route to Security Engineering. Once countersigned we'll send the final package and a short handover note for your procurement records.

-Markus Klein
VP, Product Security
Redwood Inference
